title: “Hearing the Buddha’s words, The wise monk fully understands the body, Sees it as it really is. As it is below, so above, As above,…
content:
“Hearing the Buddha’s words,
The wise monk fully understands the body,
Sees it as it really is.

As it is below, so above,
As above, so below —
Abandoning desire for the body inside and out,

The wise monk abandons desire and lust.
He attains the deathless, peace,
The constant state of Nibbāna.

This two-footed, impure, foul-smelling body
Filled with various rotting corpses, oozing —
Yet it is preserved and honored.

Who would think to exalt this body,
Or despise another —
Except one who is blind?”

title: Hemavata: “Who here has crossed the flood? Who here has crossed the ocean? Without footing, without clinging — Who does not sink into the deep?”…
content:
Hemavata:
“Who here has crossed the flood?
Who here has crossed the ocean?
Without footing, without clinging —
Who does not sink into the deep?”

The Blessed One:
“One always virtuous, wise,
Well-concentrated, inwardly directed,
Mindful — crosses the flood so hard to cross.

One who has abandoned sense-desire perceptions,
Who has overcome all fetters,
Who has destroyed delight in existence —
Does not sink into the deep.”

title: Few among humans Reach the further shore, While the rest of humankind Run up and down on this shore. Those who practice the Dhamma In…
content:
Few among humans
Reach the further shore,
While the rest of humankind
Run up and down on this shore.
Those who practice the Dhamma
In accordance with the well-taught Dhamma,
Will reach the further shore,
Beyond the realm of death, so hard to escape.
The wise, having left the dark state,
Should develop the bright,
Leaving home for the homeless life,
Living in seclusion, where pleasure is hard to find.
Seeking delight in Nibbāna,
Having abandoned sensual pleasures, without possessions,
The wise should cleanse themselves
Of defilements of the mind.
Those who have well developed the factors of enlightenment
With a mind rightly directed,
Who, without clinging, delight in the abandoning of grasping —
They, the defilement-free, the radiant,
Attain final Nibbāna in the world.

title: - What gives birth to a person? What always runs about? What undergoes rebirth? What does a person rely on? - Craving gives birth to…
content:
- What gives birth to a person?
What always runs about?
What undergoes rebirth?
What does a person rely on?
- Craving gives birth to a person,
The mind itself always runs about,
Beings undergo rebirth,
Kamma is what a person relies on.

title: “Brahmin, if an elder is eighty, ninety, or a hundred years old, and he enjoys sensual pleasures, dwells amidst sensual pleasures, is burned by the…
content: “Brahmin, if an elder is eighty, ninety, or a hundred years old, and he enjoys sensual pleasures, dwells amidst sensual pleasures, is burned by the fever of sensual pleasures, consumed by sensual thoughts, and strives for sensual pleasures — such a person is called a fool, not an elder. But if a young person, brahmin, a youth with black hair, endowed with the blessing of youth, in the prime of life, does not enjoy sensual pleasures, does not dwell amidst sensual pleasures, is not burned by the fever of sensual pleasures, not consumed by sensual thoughts, and does not strive for sensual pleasures — such a person is called a wise one, an elder.”

title: “Furthermore, monks, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis, simply because of sensuality, they engage in misconduct of body,…
content: “Furthermore, monks, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis, simply because of sensuality, they engage in misconduct of body, misconduct of speech, misconduct of mind. Having engaged in misconduct of body, speech, and mind, with the breakup of the body, after death, they are reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell. Monks, such is the peril of sensuality, leading to future suffering, a mass of suffering, with sensuality as the cause, sensuality as the source, sensuality as the basis – simply because of sensuality.”

title: “Nāgita, for those who are heavily inclined toward delight, when there is change, alteration, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise — that is the…
content: “Nāgita, for those who are heavily inclined toward delight, when there is change, alteration, sorrow, lamentation, pain, grief, and despair arise — that is the natural result. For those who fix their minds on the sign of the foul, Nāgita, disenchantment with the sign of the beautiful becomes established — that is the natural result. For one who dwells contemplating impermanence in the six sense bases, Nāgita, disenchantment with contact becomes established — that is the natural result. For one who dwells contemplating arising and passing away in the five aggregates of clinging, Nāgita, disenchantment with clinging becomes established — that is the natural result.”

title: “I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen factors of enlightenment arise and arisen factors of enlightenment come to completion, as wise…
content: “I do not see any other thing, monks, through which unarisen factors of enlightenment arise and arisen factors of enlightenment come to completion, as wise attention. Through wise attention, monks, unarisen factors of enlightenment arise and arisen factors of enlightenment come to full development.”

title: “Furthermore, Meghiya, for a monk well established in these five things, four more things are to be developed: foulness should be developed to abandon greed;…
content: “Furthermore, Meghiya, for a monk well established in these five things, four more things are to be developed: foulness should be developed to abandon greed; loving-kindness should be developed to abandon ill-will; mindfulness of breathing should be developed to cut off thoughts; the perception of impermanence should be developed to uproot the conceit ‘I am.’ For one with the perception of impermanence, Meghiya, the perception of not-self becomes established. For one with the perception of not-self, the uprooting of the conceit ‘I am’ is attained, Nibbāna in this very life.”

title: “Monks, if that monk, while attending to a different wholesome sign, still has evil, unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, ill-will, and delusion arising, then that…
content: “Monks, if that monk, while attending to a different wholesome sign, still has evil, unwholesome thoughts connected with desire, ill-will, and delusion arising, then that monk should examine the peril in those thoughts: ‘These thoughts are unwholesome, these thoughts are blameworthy, these thoughts lead to painful results.’ By examining the peril in those thoughts, those evil, unwholesome thoughts are abandoned and subside. With their abandonment, the mind becomes steadied, settled, unified, and concentrated.”
